title: Voice echo catalog and operation hypotheses (2026-06-18)
content:
Purpose: quick synthesis of frontline "echoes" (short customer quotes and small patterns) and a compact set of operational hypotheses we can run as low-effort probes. Goal is to capture high-velocity signals that aren’t yet full-feature requests but indicate repeat friction or opportunity; translate into 2-week micro-experiments or documentation patches.

Context and scope:
- Source: account exec notes, SRE incidents where customers called about inference behavior, weekly CS triage, and an ad-hoc survey run with 12 enterprise trial users (May–Jun 2026).
- Focus: inference UX (model selection, latency variability, retry behavior), cost explainability, and rollout/rollback controls in the Console.
- Tone: intentionally raw — verbatim snippets included to preserve nuance.

Quick top-3 themes (summary):
1) Surprise fallback behavior when capacity constrained -> customers see different model outputs (high severity for deterministic workflows).
   - Occurrence: called out by 6 customers (2 enterprise legal teams, 4 startups).
   - Example quote: "We got different answers mid-day — can't trust the pipeline for compliance checks."
   - Immediate pain: regression risk for deterministic evaluation; manual re-checks increase ops cost.

2) Cost per inference unclear across model variants and batch settings -> customers conservative, under-batched -> higher latency and costs.
   - Occurrence: 9 customers referenced wanting clearer unit economics to tune batching and caching.
   - Quote: "I can't justify switching to a cheaper quantized variant unless I can predict quality delta vs cost."

3) Rollouts feel all-or-nothing; customers want small-traffic canaries and fast reversion hooks that are visible.
   - Occurrence: 7 customers requested finer-grained rollout controls and transparent logs of who/when a model change occurred.

Raw snippets (verbatim samples, anonymized):
- "Our nightly job started failing — turned out the model fallback changed tokenization slightly." (startup, infra team)
- "Support said 'we routed to a compatible variant' but gave no visibility — we need the rule that chose it." (enterprise security)
- "Batching is magic? If I set batch_size=64 I see latency spikes, but cost drops — need a cheat-sheet." (platform engineer)

Affinity mapping (quick clusters):
- Visibility & Audits: explicit decision logs for routing/fallbacks, per-request lineage, who changed rollout.
- Cost Transparency: concise per-model/per-config cost estimates + recommended batch/cache knobs per workload archetype.
- Determinism & Compatibility: clear contract for variant compatibility (tokenization/IO/output formatting guarantees).

Operational hypotheses and 2-week probes (ranked by expected insight/effort):
A. "Fallback timeline" probe (effort: low, owner: Liam)
   - Hypothesis: If we add a simple per-request header explaining which model variant served the request and why (policy tag), customers will stop raising 'mystery-answer' tickets.
   - Deliverable: add header + Console toggle to show routing decisions for sample requests; instrument frequency metric (requests with fallback tag).
   - Success metric: tickets referencing unexplained fallback drop by 50% in next 30d; adoption: enable toggle by 10 customers.

B. "Economics cheat-sheet" micro-doc + sample calc (effort: very low, owner: Priya)
   - Hypothesis: Publish a 1-pager with 3 workload archetypes (chatty UI, batch embeddings, nightly eval) showing recommended batch/cache + expected cost deltas will reduce conservatism and increase trial conversions.
   - Deliverable: 1-page PDF + quick script that estimates monthly token cost for a given QPS and batch size.
   - Success metric: customer-reported confidence score (survey) improves + 5% uptick in trials toggling batching.

C. "Canary UI tweaks" interactive mock (effort: medium, owner: Jordan)
   - Hypothesis: A dedicated UI for canarying (traffic % slider, auto-revert on error threshold, visible audit trail) will reduce perceived rollout risk and increase customers' willingness to change model variants.
   - Deliverable: clickable Figma + prototype demo to 3 largest trial accounts.
   - Success metric: 2 customers adopt canary flow in next quarter; measured rollback time decreases.

D. "Compatibility contract" quick-FAQ (effort: medium, owner: Maya)
   - Hypothesis: Publishing a short compatibility rubric (what changes between variants are guaranteed vs may change) will lower incident triage time and reduce false-positive regressions.
   - Deliverable: FAQ + a few example diffs between common variants (tokenization, EOS behavior, structured output markers).
   - Success metric: number of incidents tagged 'variant-compatibility' reduced by 30%.

Low-confidence signals (callouts to validate before building):
- Request-level cost billing requested by 2 customers — heavy product effort; verify whether aggregated unit economics cheat-sheet reduces the ask.
- Some customers equate "deterministic" with identical token-level outputs — may be unrealistic for quantized variants; need to define acceptable divergence.

Next steps (concrete):
- This doc -> post to Confluence as a working note (Maya) and link to JIRA epic JIRA-CS-987.
- Run A (header + toggle) experiment within 1 sprint; add instrumentation (Liam).
- Priya to draft the Economics cheat-sheet and a sample cost calculator snippet; aim to ship as KB article.
- Jordan to mock Canary UI; schedule 30-min demos with two enterprise contacts (names in Slack thread).
- Quick survey to participating trial customers after probe A/B states to capture confidence/clarity signals.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we enable header-by-default for hosted API or leave opt-in? (tradeoff: noise vs transparency).
- Level of guarantee for "compatibility contract" — legal/regulatory implications for enterprise SLAs? (loop in security/compliance).
- Which team owns the cost calculator backend if customers ask for a hosted widget? (product ops vs optimize).

Notes to self (things to capture in Confluence):
- Include short baked examples of fallback header values and sample Console screenshots.
- Keep the Economics cheat-sheet consumable in <2 minutes reading time.
- Track all related tickets under JIRA-CS-987 and tag with 'voice-echo'.

Appendix: sample fallback header spec (proposal)
- X-Redwood-Model: redwood/v2.1.3
- X-Redwood-Variant-Policy: fallback-capacity-tier
- X-Redwood-Selected-Variant: redwood-quant-8bit
- X-Redwood-Routing-Reached: TOPOGRAPHY:zone-us-west2 / policy:latency-priority

(End of working note — preserve rawness; we'll iterate in Confluence.)
